items.title: Proposition 2.1(iii): reflection symmetry of the augmented law

source.attribution: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang. ASTIS mathematical restatement, not original prose; no endorsement implied.

items.statement: For the paper's augmented Gibbs law, reflecting the auxiliary point through the current position leaves the joint distribution unchanged. Applying this reflection twice gives the original state.
assumptions: The source works on Euclidean space with a twice continuously differentiable potential V satisfying alpha I <= Hessian V <= beta I for 0<alpha<=beta, and mu(dx)=Z^{-1} exp(-V(x)) dx.
The source takes 0<eta<=1/beta and defines the joint density proportional to exp(-V(x)-||x-y||^2/(2 eta)).
The paper also displays the generative representation: independent X~mu and Z~N(0,I), then Y=X+sqrt(eta) Z. Equality of the normalized density and this generative law is a separate formal obligation.

obligations.label: Involution and reflection invariance of the displayed generative Gaussian augmentation
Identify the normalized density (2.6) with the generative probability law (2.7) under the source hypotheses

bindings.boundary: The generative-law proof component, not the density identification or any PBPS transition/process invariance theorem.

assumption_deltas.source: The target is a strongly log-concave smooth Gibbs probability law on R^d
assumption_deltas.lean: Any probability measure on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel sigma algebra
assumption_deltas.reason: The selected symmetry calculation only uses independence and symmetry of the auxiliary standard Gaussian. Neither a density nor potential regularity enters this proof component; the density adapter remains open.
The upper step-size restriction controls other curvature and algorithmic bounds. Gaussian sign symmetry works at every positive scale; it does not establish those bounds.

assumption_deltas.source: The joint law is written by both a normalized density and a generative representation
assumption_deltas.lean: The joint law is explicitly a pushforward of mu.prod(stdGaussian E)
assumption_deltas.reason: The formalized measure is the generative representation. Identifying it with the density requires a separate normalization/change-of-variables proof.

assumption_deltas.source: The state-space maps are affine maps on Euclidean space
assumption_deltas.lean: Measurability is proved from BorelSpace, finite-dimensional topology, addition and scalar multiplication
assumption_deltas.reason: The pushforward composition rules require measurable maps. The proof supplies this prerequisite rather than treating the totalized map API as mathematical invariance.
